title: Backend entry domain db schema design
topic: Backend entry domain db schema design
question: You're designing the database schema for a simple blog: users, posts, and comments. Walk through the tables and how they relate.
idealAnswer:
Proposes a users table, a posts table with a foreign key to users (author_id), and a comments table with foreign keys to both posts and users

Correctly identifies the relationship types: one user to many posts, one post to many comments (one-to-many in both cases)

Uses a primary key (typically an auto-incrementing id or UUID) on each table, and explains foreign keys as the mechanism that enforces referential integrity between tables

Considers what happens on delete, e.g. should deleting a post cascade to delete its comments, or should it be restricted, and can explain the tradeoff

Avoids obvious normalization mistakes like duplicating the author's username on every post row instead of joining through author_id
